page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a running head at the top and a page number at the top left. Italic emblem mottos stand between the verse stanzas. A catchword sits at the lower right.

main_text.p: Lux est perpetua una contuenda: Quam Sol iustitiae parauit unus Dandam iudicij die supremi Cunctis, quos pietas fideque pura Clararint pugiles, malique mundi Victores Satanae & malignioris.
Ast his quos Satanas malus caroque Cum mundo domitat procax procaci, Nox est perpetua una transfigenda Poena in tartarea & nigris tenebris.

head.i: Mensores quod metiantur suum nil habent. Ca-thedrarij philosophi.

main_text.p: Describit radio totum qui gentibus orbem, In toto mensor possidet orbe nihil. Sic vos assueti virtutis vbique triumphos, Et laudes plenis ingeminare tubis, Turba, Sophi, mendax, nil dum virtutis habetis, Virtutis tumidos fertis in ore sonos.

Est animal, Graia dicunt quod voce Pyraustam, Aer cui vitam, lympha, foliumque negant. In mediis oritur Cypri vivitque caminis, Unus & est illi feruida flamma cibus. Diceris, & merito, par, Iracunde, Pyrausta Fellis namque focus sola fit esca tibi.

head.i: Febricitans male culpat aquas. Non aurum sed auarus culpandus.

main_text.p: Algentes caufaris aquas, quae Caufona membris, Nonnisi cum vita diffugiente, fugant.

page.notes: The catchword at the lower right is cut off by the page edge and read as "Vi" with doubt. The first word of the top line of the emblem heading "Ca-" is a hyphenated line end carried into the next line. The marks on the right edge are show-through and were left out. Several verse words are doubtful in the scan, such as "caufaris" and "viuit", and were copied as printed.
